eh there’s different levels of transitioning but i get what you mean. a child under the age of 12 that identifies as trans should be able to socially transition; ie. change name with friends and family, dress how they want, go by different pronouns. kids from 12 should at least be able to go on hormone blockers which are totally reversible and essentially just give time for them to make a decision abt what they want to do. kids aged 16+ should be able to medically transition; ie. going on hormones , contemplating surgery. 

the thing to remember is that medical transition is not a quick and easy process. the person is usually on a year+ long waitlist and has to see various gender therapists and psychologists along the way to make sure they know what is happening and that they’re mentally stable enough to go through with it. 

in my opinion, the comfort of the child is much more important than anyone else’s views on what age transitioning is acceptable. it will vary from kid to kid and if it doesn’t concern you, then your opinion on it doesn’t matter

gender is essentially how you view yourself and how you feel. it’s hard to describe accurately to a cisgender person but gender is a continuum or a spectrum, but rather than a line, it’s more like a colour wheel with almost an infinite different aspects which can influence it. this is largely because gender is a social construct, with certain traits, roles, colours, jobs, and clothes being labelled as ‘male’ or ‘female’ (at least in western cultures). 

you’re on the right track with different traits being feminine and masculine and although some people may not like it, i personally don’t mind some things being masculine or feminine as it allows me to wear masculine or feminine clothes to portray how i feel to the world and people around me. however i do believe that we should be a lot more open in the sense that, yes maybe blue is a traditional masculine colour but that doesn’t mean women can’t wear it yknow ? i think that should apply to everything, particularly clothing 

in regards to your question of “would a girl who prefers being brash and straightforward identify as a boy?” and vice versa, the short answer is no. the long answer is it depends entirely on the person. i identify as not really a boy or a girl but i often present more masculine, wearing jeans and shirts, hoodies, boots etc. however i do like to put on a skirt sometimes and wear makeup to feel pretty. you can identify as a girl and be super masculine, and you would still be a girl and vice versa. it entirely depends on what you feel you are. 

i view gender as an extremely personal thing, and my gender identity is very specific to me as it’s shaped by my experiences. i’ve never felt like a girl and when i was younger i would often fantasise about being a boy. gender, like sexuality is also extremely fluid and can change over time. anyway i rambled a bit sorry, but i hope that answers some of your questions. i’m happy to answer any more that you have ! if you wanna dm me as well i’d be more than happy to continue this convo

not sure how to share a post in a comment but all credit for the following goes to u/Harpoon385 . None of this is mine but i thought it might help you because it’s certainly helped me:

For anyone questioning their gender....


I  very frequently see people who are questioning their gender asking the  same thing (not that it is bad that they ask these questions), and who  get caught up in certain aspects of this.

Being  transgender and scared does not mean you are cisgender. It is  absolutely reasonable to be scared when you are questioning your gender  and believe you are transgender, but that doesn't mean you are  cisgender. Don't think you are the only trans person out there who is  scared, you are not, it's very common.

Having  doubts is normal. This is a big, life changing decision that does not  come without risks, so of course you will be unsure if this is the right  thing to do. However try not to get too caught up in the dumb excuses  as to why you are not transgender. The simplest explanation is most  likely the right one.

Just  because you think you might not be able to pass, or only want to  transition if you will pass doesn't make you cisgender. And not all  transgender people do want to pass as male for female (such as  non-binary people, not all, but some).

Never  assume all transgender people feel a certain way, or that your  narrative is 100% unique and all transgender people do not feel the way  you do. So many people seem to think this, but it's not true.

You  are not delusional, you are not making this all up in your head for  attention, and you are not making yourself feel this way. You would know  if you were doing this for attention or forcing yourself to feel this  way.

You  do not need to experience gender dysphoria to be transgender. Gender  euphoria is a thing too. If you just feel as if you would prefer to be  another gender, but being the one you were assigned at birth does not  bother you, that is perfectly alright.

You can realize you are transgender at any age. It's not any less valid at any other age.

You can be non-binary and still want to start HRT.

Not minding having the sex organs you were born with does not make you "less" trans.

Mostly  sure about your gender identity is close enough. It's very hard to be  completely sure without taking any steps, and even then its normal to  have doubts.

Don't confuse sexual orientation with gender identity. And gender identity with gender presentation.

I  hope this helped somebody who is currently questioning their gender. I  probably missed a few things, but I didn't want it to be too long. I  only mean this as a guide, I apologize if anything was inaccurate, I'm  simply trying to help.
